title: Ingress SLA-aware Loss Compensator and Graceful Spillover for Console Telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem summary: the current console ingest path can drop events under tenant microbursts or upstream transient failures, causing gaps in tenant-level usage analytics and SLA violations. We need an ingress component that preserves latency SLOs for high-priority traffic while compensating for best-effort traffic loss through bounded buffering, deterministic replay markers, and prioritized spillover policies. This ticket implements an SLA-aware loss compensator placed in the edge ingress layer that performs tenant-aware admission, in-memory micro-reservoir buffering, idempotent batch sequencing, and a best-effort persistent spill queue for delayed replay.
background: Existing work has explored hotkey mitigation and tenant prescaling (see ENG-950401, ENG-111111). However those approaches focus on prescaling and admission control upstream; they do not provide bounded compensatory buffering when bursts exceed capacity or when downstream processing temporarily slows. Customer-facing dashboards and billing rely on accurate counts; we need graceful degradation rather than silent loss. This design aims to minimize memory amplification, keep tail latency within SLOs, and provide deterministic reconciliation for eventual completeness.
acceptance_criteria:
- Component deployed behind the ingress gateway and can be toggled via feature flag per-region.
- For P0 routes, 99th percentile tail-add latency (ingress handler) must remain <= 80ms under tested microburst scenarios.
- Under simulated downstream outage (30s), no more than 1% of P0 events are dropped; P1/P2 events may be degraded per policy.
- Buffered events are replayed within configured retention window (default 5 minutes) and deduplicated by sequence tokens.
- Metrics emitted: buffered_events_count, spill_queue_depth, replay_success_rate, rejection_rate_by_reason. Dashboards linked in notes.
design_decisions:
- Bounded micro-reservoir per-tenant sized by recent QPS and priority tiers to avoid global memory exhaustion.
- Admission classification: P0 (latency-critical), P1 (analytics-critical), P2 (best-effort). Only P0 gets guaranteed in-memory reservation; P1 can use opportunistic reservation; P2 flows to spill queue directly when capacity exceeded.
- Use monotonic ingestion sequence tokens from edge to enable idempotent replay and exact-once best-effort semantics when downstream dedup supports token-based de-duplication.
- Spill queue persisted to a per-region compacted append store (rocks-backed local queue) with TTL and backoff-based drain.
- Backpressure policy: degrade P2 -> P1 -> P0 order configurable; default preserves P0 at cost of P2.
- Safety: lease-based fence to avoid double-replay during failover; checkpoints exported to central metadata store for visibility.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype micro-reservoir allocator library and unit tests (2d). 2) Add admission and tenant-priority classifier to ingress (3d). 3) Integrate local persistent spill queue with dedupe metadata (4d). 4) Hook replay worker with exponential backoff and metrics (3d). 5) Add feature flag + config surface in Console and rollout config (1d). 6) End-to-end load-tests and chaos injection to validate behavior (3d). 7) Gradual region-by-region rollout (see rollout_plan).
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal canary in staging with synthetic tenant microbursts. Phase B: enable for low-traffic region, observe metrics for 48h. Phase C: enable for 10% production routes, monitor replay_success_rate and rejection_rate. If any P0 tail latency regression > 5% rollback immediately. Full rollout after two weeks stable in multiple regions.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Emit and dashboard the following metrics: ingress.buffered_events_total, ingress.spill_queue_depth, ingress.replay_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99, ingress.rejection_rate_by_priority, ingress.lease_conflicts.
Alerts:
- P0 rejection_rate > 0.1% sustained 5m -> Sev2.
- replay_success_rate < 95% over 15m -> Sev2.
- spill_queue_depth > configured_threshold -> Pager.
Logs include tenant id, admission action, sequence token, and reason for rejection.
testing:
Unit tests for allocator behavior under concurrent allocation/free.
Integration tests for replay correctness with dedup enabled.
Load test scenarios: steady-state 10k rps, microburst 200x for 10s, gradual downstream slowdown to emulate GC pauses and network flaps.
Chaos tests: failover of ingress node during replay, out-of-order replay injection.
Add regression test to CI harness referencing synthetic datasets.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: micro-reservoir sizing may under/over-provision -> mitigation: conservative default and telemetry to auto-tune; implement OOM guards and tenant-level caps.
- Risk: persisted spill queue could become hotspot -> mitigation: region-sharded queues and backpressure to admission.
- Risk: dedupe metadata growth -> mitigation: compact by checkpointing and TTL; keep token space small and rotate periodically.
- Risk: complexity of lease fencing -> mitigation: reuse existing lease primitives from ingestion lease manager and add thorough testing.
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Ingress+SLA-Aware+Loss+Compensator (internal). Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/482 (WIP). Related tickets: ENG-950401 (tenant prescaling), ENG-111111 (hotkey fairness). Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ingest-compensator (internal).
